content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: fuller staffing push lifts service level to 73.8% for 12:45-14:45 (vs 58.1% with no action) at ₹1,164. It is still short of the 80% target, but it is the best plan that follows policy.","why":"Handle time on general has jumped to 646 s against about 350–376 s forecast. The cause is CRM customer search slowness (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862). Volume and staffing are near plan. No policy-compliant plan reaches 80%, so the code picked the strongest compliant option. R1 delays both break windows, adds overtime (5 payments agents and 2 general agents), runs IVR callback on both queues to 15:00, and adds 20% chat deflection from 14:30. Predicted results for the window: payments 71.7%, general 76.4%, abandon rate 6.6% (vs 9.3% with no action). Rest of day is predicted at 87.1%.","trade_offs":["Cost: R1 costs ₹1,164. P4 costs ₹804 and reaches 69.2%. P3 costs ₹540 and reaches 65.7%. The no-cost P1 reaches only 64.6%. R1 buys roughly 4.6 more points than P4 for ₹360.","Customer impact: R1 has the lowest compliant abandon rate at 6.6%, vs 7.8–9.8% for the other compliant plans. It does rely on callbacks and chat deflection, so some customers will not get a live answer straight away.","Queue balance: payments is the weaker queue in every plan. R1 lifts payments from 52.8% to 71.7% without hurting general, which goes from 65.0% to 76.4%.","Not chosen: R2 would reach 75.6% at the same cost. It breaks policy CX-01, because the refund-status outage message targets a reason that is not rising on payments.","Agent impact: R1 delays both break windows by 45 minutes and depends on 7 agents accepting overtime."],"watch":"Watch overtime acceptance, especially the 5 payments agents; if fewer accept, payments will fall short of 71.7%. Track progress on the CRM incident, because the plan assumes slowness lasts until about 14:45. If the fix comes early, release the overtime. If slowness runs past 14:45, re-plan."}
